destroy-supported-units skips units now owned by the capturer, which civ1-unit's defecting-units has moved over for an incited city (civ-clone/web-renderer#58). A conquest leaves none, so nothing changes there.
Through civ1-unit's defecting-units and this package's capture rules (Copilot, on #8). Needs civ-clone/civ1-unit's fix for it, which homes them in no city.
A Captured rule unregisters the city's AdvanceStolen records, as v474.05 clears its TechnologyStolen flag in CityTakeover (civ-clone/web-renderer#58).
Also #66: the standard pnpm workflow, prettier --check, and no yarn lock.
From v474.05 (civ-clone/web-renderer#58):

actions, for a Diplomat (not a Caravan) next to a rival city, not from a ship: steal-technology (once per city, with something to take), industrial-sabotage, incite-revolt (not a capital); at peace sneak-steal-technology, sneak-incite-revolt and subvert-city (double the cost); bribe-unit on a lone foreign unit outside a city, at peace or not;

lib/diplomatCosts: inciteCost ((gold + 1000) / (distance + 3) * size, halved in disorder) and bribeCost ((gold + 750) / (distance + 2) * cost / 10, halved unless Settlers), distance to the nearest Palace capped at 16;

Rules/Unit/diplomat: the effects. Steal picks uniformly among the victim's advances the thief lacks and records AdvanceStolen; sabotage destroys a random improvement (never the Palace or a Wonder) half the time or when the box is empty, else empties the box; incite pays and captures the city with the action as the cause; bribe pays and transfers the unit, homed in the nearest city if it is the briber's. Each emits an event;
Rules/City/captured: defecting-units (High) moves the old owner's units in the city and on adjacent non-city tiles over to the inciter;
Rules/Unit/transferred: a transferred unit loses Veteran and Fortified and has no moves; emits unit:transferred;
break-peace-treaty applies to any action with an enemy().

The transferred rule clears the unit's turns-aloft note, as v474.05 recreates a bribed or defecting unit: a Bomber a turn out when it was bribed was lost at the end of the briber's turn, before its new owner could move it (Copilot, on #15). The rule now takes the StrategyNoteRegistry.

A captured city loses a citizen, so an incited city of size 1 is destroyed, and its Destroyed rules disbanded the units it had just brought over, which were homed in it. defecting-units now homes them in the city only if it will survive, and leaves them with no home otherwise: v474.05 never destroys an incited city, and keeps the units that come over (Copilot, on civ-clone/civ1-city#8; civ-clone/web-renderer#58). The rule takes the CityGrowthRegistry.

capture(player, cause = null) passes the cause to the Captured rules as a fourth argument, so a ruleset can tell an incited city from a conquered one (civ-clone/web-renderer#58). Existing rules ignore it. Version 0.1.19.

transfer(player, city = null) sets the owner and home city and processes a new Transferred rule [Unit, Player, Player], keeping the unit (its id, its cargo, references to it) rather than destroying and recreating it, as a bribed or defecting unit needs (civ-clone/web-renderer#58). Version 0.1.25.
transfer() now applies setCity's rule: a city that isn't the new owner's leaves the unit with no home, rather than homed in someone else's city (Copilot, on #2).

Re-exports StealTechnology, SneakStealTechnology, IndustrialSabotage, InciteRevolt, SneakInciteRevolt, SubvertCity and BribeUnit from their new base-unit-action-* packages (civ-clone/web-renderer#58). Version 0.1.8.

actionsToTake drops sabotage, incite, subvert and bribe, as v474.05's computer players only steal from cities (civ-clone/web-renderer#58); SneakStealTechnology waits for shouldAttack, as SneakAttack does. library-unit ^0.1.8.

The decision moveUnit makes for a tile (the first action the AI takes, unless it breaks a treaty with a player it shouldn't attack) is now actionToTake, and it's tested both ways for SneakStealTechnology (Copilot, on #31).
